record.original_question: Let P be a planar n-point set that spans only O(n/sqrt(log n)) distinct distances. Prove or disprove that the additive energy E(P)=|{(a,b,c,d) in P^4 : a+b=c+d}| must be large.

evidence.quote: A standard reference for further reading about these concep ts is the book of Tao and Vu [57]. Nets Katz stated the following problem, suggesting that it m ight be an approach for characterizing planar point sets that span few distinct dis tances (Problem 2). Problem 34. Prove or disprove: If is a set P of n points in R2 spans O(n/ √ log n) distinct distances, then E(P) is large. 15

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, define the additive energy of $P$ by
$$E(P)=\#\{(a,b,c,d)\in P^4 : a+b=c+d\},$$
where addition is the usual vector addition in $\mathbb{R}^2$. The number of distinct distances determined by $P$ is $D(P)=\#\{\,\|p-q\|: p,q\in P,\ p\neq q\,\}$.

Prove or disprove the following statement: there exist absolute constants $c>0$ and $\alpha>0$ such that, for every $n$ and every $n$-point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with
$$D(P)=O\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}\right),$$
one has
$$E(P)\ \ge\ c\, n^{2+\alpha}.$$
(Equivalently: must any planar $n$-point set spanning only $O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ distinct distances have "large" additive energy?)
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the problem (attributed to Nets Katz) restated in the distinct-distances open-problems compendium and discussed in related works on Cartesian products with few distinct distances and on planar sets with forbidden 4-point patterns. None of the located references claim to resolve Katz's conjecture for general planar point sets; partial results address only special configurations (e.g., Cartesian products). The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Additive Structure of Cartesian Products Spanning Few Distinct Distances
status_evidence.snippet: Studies additive structure of Cartesian product point sets spanning few distinct distances, addressing a special case of Katz's question.
status_evidence.claim: Only the Cartesian-product special case has been addressed; the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Planar point sets with forbidden 4-point patterns and few distinct distances
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs planar point sets spanning few distinct distances while avoiding certain 4-point configurations; does not address additive energy lower bounds for general such sets.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on related distinct-distances structure does not resolve Katz's additive-energy problem.
